full_judgment: 10. In the case of Munshi Tamizuddin Howladar and others Vs. Altafuddin Moral and others reported in 20 DLR page 901 it has been held by a Single Bench of this Court that there is no proper service if the court fails to examine the peon and to satisfy itself as to the service under Order 5 rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Again in the case of Most. Johara Begum Vs. Rafiqul Kader reported in 25 DLR page 91 it has been held by another Single Bench of this Court that provisions rule 19 cannot be treated as a dead latter or obsolete but that the provisions of rule is mandatory and the same must be complied with due diligence, and that in the absence of declaration made and subscribe bed by the process server, as required by the rules, the service return cannot be accepted as evidence of due service. In this case it has further been held that in the absence of an inquiry made by the court as provided in rule 19 and distinct declaration of due service recorded, there is no presumption of service of summons.
